paragraphs: Rav Acha bar Uya is mentioned in Pesachim 33b. Hyman says that Seder HaDorot conflates Avya and Uya, whom he considers unrelated.

notes.text: The frozen acronym is סה״ר and is not expanded here. The source explicitly rejects conflating אויא and עויא; no identity merge is made.

The saved named Warsaw 1878–1882 Seder HaDorot, Tanaim and Amoraim 261:1 lists Acha bar Avya under Avya and raises a one-or-two-figures question. This supplies a candidate comparison for Hyman’s criticism but does not establish the source initials סה״ר or prove the full alleged conflation. No separate snippet is adopted. Hyman’s rejection of equating Avya and Uya remains his scholarly judgment, not a new authority merge.

Hyman (vol. III, p. 970) prints סה״ד, where the supplied Hebrew has סה״ר. The Hebrew text of Pesachim 33b calls the sage Rav Acha bar Rav Uya (עויא); the Davidson English reads “Avya.” Seder HaDorot 261:1 lists Rav Acha bar Avya and raises the question of one or two figures called Avya. Its list at 1828:11 names both Rav Acha bar Avira and Rav Acha bar Uya. These readings leave Hyman’s judgment about the names as his own.
